# Semiconductor crystal growing, zone refining and doping (`semiconductor_purification`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/electricity.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Electricity & electronics (`electricity`)
- Deps: helped by crystal_detector, periodic_table
- Core idea: A device needs control over the concentration of electrically active impurities. The starting crystal must be pure enough for the intended dopant to determine its behaviour. Zone refining: move a narrow molten zone slowly along a bar of germanium or silicon, for instance with a ring-shaped induction heater; many impurities prefer the melt and are swept to one end, and repeated passes multiply the effect. Crystal pulling: dip a small seed crystal into the melt and withdraw it slowly while turning it, so that the melt freezes on as one continuous crystal, with the dopant added to the melt. Junctions are then made by letting dopant vapour diffuse a few thousandths of a millimetre into the hot solid surface. Germanium melts at 938 °C, silicon at 1,414 °C, and molten silicon attacks most crucibles, so it is refined as a rod held without a crucible (float zone).
- Pitfalls:
  - Relying on a single bulk purity figure. Different contaminants affect carrier concentration and lifetime by different amounts
  - Accepting polycrystalline ingots because they are easier; this was the majority view at Bell Labs in 1948 and Teal had to grow crystals almost against orders
  - Contaminating the crystal again in handling: copper, gold and sodium from tools, water and fingers are poison
  - Silicon tetrachloride, silane, arsenic and phosphorus compounds used in the process are toxic, corrosive or self-igniting
- History: europe: 1916–1918 – Czochralski's crystal-pulling method for metals (Berlin); 1954 Emeis independently develops crucible-free float zoning at Siemens; americas: 1948 – Teal and Little pull single crystals of germanium at Bell Labs; 1951 Pfann's zone refining; 1951 measurements on silicon single crystals by McSkimin, Bond, Buehler and Teal. In 1952 Teal and Buehler report grown silicon junctions and Theuerer files his float-zone patent. Keck and Golay publish independent float-zone work in 1953; 1954–1956 Fuller's diffusion of dopants
- Read:
  - H. J. McSkimin, W. L. Bond, E. Buehler & G. K. Teal, Measurement of the Elastic Constants of Silicon Single Crystals and Their Thermal Coefficients, Physical Review 83 (1951)
  - William G. Pfann, Zone Melting (1958)
  - P. H. Keck & M. J. E. Golay, Crystallization of Silicon from a Floating Liquid Zone, Physical Review 89 (1953)
  - Michael Riordan & Lillian Hoddeson, Crystal Fire: The Birth of the Information Age (1997)
